criteria.criterion: whether the class shares count hours or persons, read against the published labour services index
criteria.detail: 7,161 adjacent-year steps inside one section and country. Reproducing the published labour services index as the total plus the class term: with HOURS as the total, rmse 0.00108, correlation +0.9998, within 1e-3 in 6,972; with PERSONS, rmse 0.03284, correlation +0.8370, within 1e-3 in 479. Dropping the class term entirely gives 0.02033 and 0.03765, so the class shares are doing work in both. The reading is HOURS, by a factor of 30.33 in root mean square error. PASS records that the two readings are far enough apart to tell them apart at all.
criteria.name: B106-9

criteria.criterion: what the verdict changes about the field's reading
criteria.detail: the difference between the two totals is the change in hours per worker, and it is not small: sd 0.0325 against 0.0569 for hours and 0.0441 for persons, correlation between the two totals +0.8221. So the two readings are genuinely different objects and the verdict above is load bearing. With the verdict at HOURS, the field is relative HOURLY pay and part-time composition is not an alternative for any of the leftover.
